++	/* --- Test 3: cursor movement ----------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[10;5HPositioned here\r\n", -1);
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_02_cursor.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 4: erase --------------------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[2J\033[H", -1);  /* clear screen, home */
++	term_feed(ts, "Screen cleared!\r\n", -1);
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[44m\033[37m Blue background white text \033[0m\r\n", -1);
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_03_erase.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 5: scroll -------------------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[2J\033[H", -1);
++	for (int i = 0; i &lt; rows + 5; i++) {
++		char line[64];
++		int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "Line %d\r\n", i + 1);
++		term_feed(ts, line, n);
++	}
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_04_scroll.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 6: colour matrix ------------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[2J\033[H", -1);
++	for (int fg = 30; fg &lt;= 37; fg++) {
++		for (int bg = 40; bg &lt;= 47; bg++) {
++			char seq[32];
++			int n = snprintf(seq, sizeof(seq), "\033[%d;%dm#", fg, bg);
++			term_feed(ts, seq, n);
++		}
++		term_feed(ts, "\033[0m\r\n", -1);
++	}
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_05_matrix.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 7: erase in line ------------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[2J\033[H", -1);
++	term_feed(ts, "AAAAAAAAAA\r\n", -1);
++	term_feed(ts, "BBBBBBBBBB\033[5D\033[K\r\n", -1); /* erase last 5 */
++	term_feed(ts, "CCCCCCCCCC\r\n", -1);
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_06_erase_line.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 8: bold/bright colors -------------------------------- */
++	term_feed(ts, "\033[2J\033[H", -1);
++	for (int i = 0; i &lt; 8; i++) {
++		char seq[64];
++		snprintf(seq, sizeof(seq), "\033[%dm Normal%d ", 30 + i, i);
++		term_feed(ts, seq, -1);
++		snprintf(seq, sizeof(seq), "\033[1;%dm Bold%d \033[0m\r\n", 30 + i, i);
++		term_feed(ts, seq, -1);
++	}
++	snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_07_bold.png");
++
++	/* --- Test 9: real PTY + shell command execution (the requested case) */
++	/* This actually spawns a shell, "types" a command into it via the PTY,
++	 * lets the shell execute it, reads the real output, feeds it through
++	 * the parser, renders it, and takes a screenshot.
++	 * This proves: input received → executed in real shell → result shown.
++	 */
++	{
++		int master_fd;
++		if (open_pty_and_fork(&amp;master_fd, cols, rows) &lt; 0) {
++			fprintf(stderr, "test_terminal: PTY shell failed\n");
++		} else {
++			ts-&gt;pty_fd = master_fd;
++
++			/* Wait for initial shell prompt */
++			usleep(200 * 1000);
++			{
++				char buf[4096];
++				ssize_t n = read(master_fd, buf, sizeof(buf));
++				if (n &gt; 0) term_feed(ts, buf, (int)n);
++			}
++			snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_08_shell_prompt.png");
++
++			/* Send a real command (as if the user typed it and pressed enter) */
++			const char *cmd = "echo '=== REAL SHELL OUTPUT ==='\n";
++			write(master_fd, cmd, strlen(cmd));
++
++			/* Read the shell's response */
++			int total = 0;
++			for (int i = 0; i &lt; 20; i++) {
++				struct pollfd pfd = { .fd = master_fd, .events = POLLIN };
++				if (poll(&amp;pfd, 1, 80) &lt;= 0) break;
++				char buf[4096];
++				ssize_t n = read(master_fd, buf, sizeof(buf));
++				if (n &gt; 0) {
++					term_feed(ts, buf, (int)n);
++					total += (int)n;
++				} else {
++					break;
++				}
++			}
++
++			snap(ctx, img, ts, width, height, "term_09_real_command.png");
++
++			/* Verify the result text is present in the cell grid */
++			int found = 0;
++			const char *needle = "REAL SHELL OUTPUT";
++			for (int r = 0; r &lt; rows; r++) {
++				for (int c = 0; c &lt; cols; c++) {
++					int match = 1;
++					for (size_t k = 0; k &lt; strlen(needle); k++) {
++						if ((size_t)c + k &gt;= (size_t)cols) { match = 0; break; }
++						if (ts-&gt;cells[r * cols + c + k].ch != needle[k]) {
++							match = 0;
++							break;
++						}
++					}
++					if (match) { found = 1; break; }
++				}
++				if (found) break;
++			}
++
++			printf("Real PTY shell test: sent command, read %d bytes, result '%s' visible: %s\n",
++			       total, needle, found ? "YES" : "NO");
++
++			close(master_fd);
++		}
++	}
++
++	printf("test_terminal complete. PNG frames written.\n");
++
++	free(img-&gt;data.image.pixels);
++	img-&gt;data.image.pixels = NULL;
++	term_destroy(ts);
++	bgtk_destroy_mock(ctx);
++	return 0;
++}
+</pre>

+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-06T18:47:23-03:00
+
+    settings: do not full-redraw on mouse motion.
+
+    Ignore EV_REL/EV_ABS and only call bgtk_draw_widgets when the input
+    handler requests a redraw, matching launcher and other apps.
+
+<a href=tree-8951caa.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/apps/settings.c b/apps/settings.c
+index d192b8b..2cf6b6b 100644
+--- a/apps/settings.c
++++ b/apps/settings.c
+@@ -914,10 +914,17 @@ int main(void)
+ 	struct BGCEMessage msg;
+ 	while (bgce_recv_msg(conn, &amp;msg) &gt; 0) {
+ 		if (msg.type == MSG_INPUT_EVENT) {
+-			bgtk_handle_input_event(c, msg.data.input_event);
+-			bgtk_draw_widgets(c);
++			/* Ignore pure pointer motion — redrawing every move
++			 * freezes the UI under hover. Only key/button (and
++			 * wheel, handled inside widgets) need handling. */
++			if (msg.data.input_event.type == EV_REL ||
++			    msg.data.input_event.type == EV_ABS)
++				continue;
++			if (bgtk_handle_input_event(c, msg.data.input_event))
++				bgtk_draw_widgets(c);
+ 		} else if (msg.type == MSG_FOCUS_CHANGE) {
+ 			bgtk_set_window_focus(c, msg.data.focus_event.state);
++			/* set_window_focus already redraws */
+ 		} else if (msg.type == MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE) {
+ 			if (bgtk_handle_buffer_change(c, &amp;msg.data.buffer_reply) == 0)
+ 				bgtk_draw_widgets(c);
+</pre>

+diff --git a/apps/sys_status.c b/apps/sys_status.c
+new file mode 100644
+index 0000000..5474aaf
+--- /dev/null
++++ b/apps/sys_status.c
+@@ -0,0 +1,891 @@
++/* apps/sys_status.c
++ *
++ * System status dashboard for BGCE/BGTK.
++ * Shows clock, uptime, CPU, memory, swap, disk, internet, and weather.
++ *
++ * Build (Linux):  make sys_status
++ * Headless test:  make test_sys_status &amp;&amp; ./test_sys_status
++ */
++
++#include &lt;ctype.h&gt;
++#include &lt;errno.h&gt;
++#include &lt;netdb.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
++#include &lt;string.h&gt;
++#include &lt;time.h&gt;
++#include &lt;unistd.h&gt;
++
++#include &lt;arpa/inet.h&gt;
++#include &lt;fcntl.h&gt;
++#include &lt;netinet/in.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/socket.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/statvfs.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/time.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/types.h&gt;
++
++#if defined(__APPLE__)
++#include &lt;mach/mach.h&gt;
++#include &lt;mach/processor_info.h&gt;
++#include &lt;mach/mach_host.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/mount.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/sysctl.h&gt;
++#else
++#include &lt;sys/sysinfo.h&gt;
++#endif
++
++#include &lt;linux/input.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/mman.h&gt;
++
++#include "bgtk.h"
++#include "internal.h"
++
++/* Bootstrap buffer only — final size is measured from content. */
++#define BOOT_W 640
++#define BOOT_H 400
++#define N_ROWS 8
++#define BGCE_BPP 4
++
++enum {
++	ROW_CLOCK = 0,
++	ROW_UPTIME,
++	ROW_CPU,
++	ROW_MEM,
++	ROW_SWAP,
++	ROW_DISK,
++	ROW_NET,
++	ROW_WEATHER
++};
++
++static const char *row_names[N_ROWS] = {
++	"Clock", "Uptime", "CPU", "Memory", "Swap", "Disk /", "Internet", "Weather"
++};
++
++static struct BGTK_Context *ctx;
++static struct BGTK_Widget *name_labels[N_ROWS];
++static struct BGTK_Widget *value_labels[N_ROWS];
++static struct BGTK_Widget *row_widgets[N_ROWS];
++static struct BGTK_Widget *root_list;
++
++/* CPU sample for delta % */
++static unsigned long long cpu_idle_prev, cpu_total_prev;
++static int cpu_have_prev;
++
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++/* Formatting helpers                                                  */
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++
++static void fmt_bytes(char *out, size_t n, unsigned long long bytes)
++{
++	const double kb = 1024.0, mb = kb * 1024.0, gb = mb * 1024.0;
++	double b = (double)bytes;
++
++	if (b &gt;= gb)
++		snprintf(out, n, "%.1f GB", b / gb);
++	else if (b &gt;= mb)
++		snprintf(out, n, "%.0f MB", b / mb);
++	else if (b &gt;= kb)
++		snprintf(out, n, "%.0f KB", b / kb);
++	else
++		snprintf(out, n, "%llu B", bytes);
++}
++
++static void fmt_bar(char *out, size_t n, int pct)
++{
++	/* 10-char bar */
++	int i, filled;
++
++	if (pct &lt; 0)
++		pct = 0;
++	if (pct &gt; 100)
++		pct = 100;
++	filled = (pct + 5) / 10;
++	out[0] = '[';
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; 10; i++)
++		out[1 + i] = (i &lt; filled) ? '#' : '-';
++	out[11] = ']';
++	out[12] = '\0';
++	(void)n;
++}
++
++static void set_label_text(struct BGTK_Widget *w, const char *s)
++{
++	if (!w || !s)
++		return;
++	if (w-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_TEXT) {
++		free(w-&gt;data.text.text);
++		w-&gt;data.text.text = strdup(s);
++	} else if (w-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL &amp;&amp; w-&gt;data.label.set_label) {
++		w-&gt;data.label.set_label(w, (char *)s);
++	}
++}
++
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++/* Metrics                                                             */
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++
++static void metric_clock(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	time_t now = time(NULL);
++	struct tm tm;
++
++	localtime_r(&amp;now, &amp;tm);
++	strftime(out, n, "%a %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", &amp;tm);
++}
++
++static void metric_uptime(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	unsigned long sec = 0;
++	unsigned long d, h, m;
++
++#if defined(__APPLE__)
++	struct timeval boot;
++	size_t len = sizeof(boot);
++	if (sysctlbyname("kern.boottime", &amp;boot, &amp;len, NULL, 0) == 0) {
++		time_t now = time(NULL);
++		if (now &gt; boot.tv_sec)
++			sec = (unsigned long)(now - boot.tv_sec);
++	}
++#else
++	struct sysinfo si;
++	if (sysinfo(&amp;si) == 0)
++		sec = (unsigned long)si.uptime;
++#endif
++	d = sec / 86400;
++	h = (sec / 3600) % 24;
++	m = (sec / 60) % 60;
++	if (d &gt; 0)
++		snprintf(out, n, "%lud %luh %lum", d, h, m);
++	else if (h &gt; 0)
++		snprintf(out, n, "%luh %lum %lus", h, m, sec % 60);
++	else
++		snprintf(out, n, "%lum %lus", m, sec % 60);
++}
++
++#if defined(__APPLE__)
++static int cpu_sample_mac(unsigned long long *idle, unsigned long long *total)
++{
++	natural_t count = 0;
++	processor_info_array_t info = NULL;
++	mach_msg_type_number_t info_count = 0;
++	unsigned long long i_sum = 0, t_sum = 0;
++	unsigned int i;
++
++	if (host_processor_info(mach_host_self(), PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO,
++				&amp;count, &amp;info, &amp;info_count) != KERN_SUCCESS)
++		return -1;
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; count; i++) {
++		processor_cpu_load_info_data_t *c =
++			(processor_cpu_load_info_data_t *)info + i;
++		unsigned long long user = c-&gt;cpu_ticks[CPU_STATE_USER];
++		unsigned long long sys = c-&gt;cpu_ticks[CPU_STATE_SYSTEM];
++		unsigned long long idle_t = c-&gt;cpu_ticks[CPU_STATE_IDLE];
++		unsigned long long nice = c-&gt;cpu_ticks[CPU_STATE_NICE];
++		i_sum += idle_t;
++		t_sum += user + sys + idle_t + nice;
++	}
++	vm_deallocate(mach_task_self(), (vm_address_t)info,
++		      info_count * sizeof(integer_t));
++	*idle = i_sum;
++	*total = t_sum;
++	return 0;
++}
++#else
++static int cpu_sample_linux(unsigned long long *idle, unsigned long long *total)
++{
++	FILE *f = fopen("/proc/stat", "r");
++	unsigned long long u, n, s, id, io, irq, sirq, st;
++	char line[256];
++
++	if (!f)
++		return -1;
++	if (!fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
++		fclose(f);
++		return -1;
++	}
++	fclose(f);
++	/* cpu  user nice system idle iowait irq softirq steal ... */
++	if (sscanf(line, "cpu %llu %llu %llu %llu %llu %llu %llu %llu",
++		   &amp;u, &amp;n, &amp;s, &amp;id, &amp;io, &amp;irq, &amp;sirq, &amp;st) &lt; 4)
++		return -1;
++	*idle = id + io;
++	*total = u + n + s + id + io + irq + sirq + st;
++	return 0;
++}
++#endif
++
++static void metric_cpu(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	unsigned long long idle = 0, total = 0;
++	int pct = 0;
++	char bar[16];
++
++#if defined(__APPLE__)
++	if (cpu_sample_mac(&amp;idle, &amp;total) != 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "n/a");
++		return;
++	}
++#else
++	if (cpu_sample_linux(&amp;idle, &amp;total) != 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "n/a");
++		return;
++	}
++#endif
++	if (cpu_have_prev &amp;&amp; total &gt; cpu_total_prev) {
++		unsigned long long d_tot = total - cpu_total_prev;
++		unsigned long long d_idle = idle - cpu_idle_prev;
++		if (d_tot &gt; 0)
++			pct = (int)((d_tot - d_idle) * 100ull / d_tot);
++	} else {
++		pct = -1;
++	}
++	cpu_idle_prev = idle;
++	cpu_total_prev = total;
++	cpu_have_prev = 1;
++
++	if (pct &lt; 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "sampling…");
++		return;
++	}
++	fmt_bar(bar, sizeof(bar), pct);
++	snprintf(out, n, "%d%%  %s", pct, bar);
++}
++
++static void metric_mem_swap(char *mem_out, size_t mn, char *swap_out, size_t sn)
++{
++	unsigned long long mem_total = 0, mem_used = 0;
++	unsigned long long swap_total = 0, swap_used = 0;
++	char tbuf[32], ubuf[32], bar[16];
++	int pct;
++
++#if defined(__APPLE__)
++	{
++		int mib[2] = { CTL_HW, HW_MEMSIZE };
++		uint64_t memsize = 0;
++		size_t len = sizeof(memsize);
++		mach_msg_type_number_t count = HOST_VM_INFO64_COUNT;
++		vm_statistics64_data_t vm;
++
++		sysctl(mib, 2, &amp;memsize, &amp;len, NULL, 0);
++		mem_total = memsize;
++		if (host_statistics64(mach_host_self(), HOST_VM_INFO64,
++				      (host_info64_t)&amp;vm, &amp;count) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
++			/* active + wired ≈ used; inactive freeable */
++			uint64_t page = (uint64_t)sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
++			mem_used = (uint64_t)(vm.active_count + vm.wire_count) * page;
++			swap_total = 0;
++			swap_used = 0;
++			/* xsw_usage for swap */
++			struct xsw_usage xsw;
++			len = sizeof(xsw);
++			if (sysctlbyname("vm.swapusage", &amp;xsw, &amp;len, NULL, 0) == 0) {
++				swap_total = xsw.xsu_total;
++				swap_used = xsw.xsu_used;
++			}
++		} else {
++			mem_used = 0;
++		}
++	}
++#else
++	{
++		FILE *f = fopen("/proc/meminfo", "r");
++		char key[64];
++		unsigned long val;
++		unsigned long mem_total_k = 0, mem_avail_k = 0, mem_free_k = 0;
++		unsigned long buffers_k = 0, cached_k = 0;
++		unsigned long swap_total_k = 0, swap_free_k = 0;
++		char line[256];
++
++		if (f) {
++			while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
++				if (sscanf(line, "%63[^:]: %lu", key, &amp;val) != 2)
++					continue;
++				if (!strcmp(key, "MemTotal"))
++					mem_total_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "MemAvailable"))
++					mem_avail_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "MemFree"))
++					mem_free_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "Buffers"))
++					buffers_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "Cached"))
++					cached_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "SwapTotal"))
++					swap_total_k = val;
++				else if (!strcmp(key, "SwapFree"))
++					swap_free_k = val;
++			}
++			fclose(f);
++		}
++		mem_total = mem_total_k * 1024ull;
++		if (mem_avail_k)
++			mem_used = (mem_total_k - mem_avail_k) * 1024ull;
++		else
++			mem_used = (mem_total_k - mem_free_k - buffers_k - cached_k) *
++				   1024ull;
++		swap_total = swap_total_k * 1024ull;
++		swap_used = (swap_total_k - swap_free_k) * 1024ull;
++	}
++#endif
++
++	fmt_bytes(ubuf, sizeof(ubuf), mem_used);
++	fmt_bytes(tbuf, sizeof(tbuf), mem_total);
++	pct = mem_total ? (int)(mem_used * 100ull / mem_total) : 0;
++	fmt_bar(bar, sizeof(bar), pct);
++	snprintf(mem_out, mn, "%s / %s (%d%%) %s", ubuf, tbuf, pct, bar);
++
++	fmt_bytes(ubuf, sizeof(ubuf), swap_used);
++	fmt_bytes(tbuf, sizeof(tbuf), swap_total);
++	pct = swap_total ? (int)(swap_used * 100ull / swap_total) : 0;
++	if (swap_total == 0)
++		snprintf(swap_out, sn, "none");
++	else {
++		fmt_bar(bar, sizeof(bar), pct);
++		snprintf(swap_out, sn, "%s / %s (%d%%) %s", ubuf, tbuf, pct, bar);
++	}
++}
++
++static void metric_disk(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	struct statvfs st;
++	unsigned long long total, used, free_b;
++	char tbuf[32], ubuf[32], bar[16];
++	int pct;
++
++	if (statvfs("/", &amp;st) != 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "n/a (%s)", strerror(errno));
++		return;
++	}
++	total = (unsigned long long)st.f_blocks * st.f_frsize;
++	free_b = (unsigned long long)st.f_bavail * st.f_frsize;
++	used = total &gt; free_b ? total - free_b : 0;
++	pct = total ? (int)(used * 100ull / total) : 0;
++	fmt_bytes(ubuf, sizeof(ubuf), used);
++	fmt_bytes(tbuf, sizeof(tbuf), total);
++	fmt_bar(bar, sizeof(bar), pct);
++	snprintf(out, n, "%s / %s (%d%%) %s", ubuf, tbuf, pct, bar);
++}
++
++/* Non-blocking-ish TCP connect with short timeout to a public DNS. */
++static void metric_internet(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	int fd;
++	struct sockaddr_in addr;
++	struct timeval tv0, tv1;
++	int flags, err = 0;
++	socklen_t elen = sizeof(err);
++	fd_set wfds;
++	struct timeval tv;
++	long ms;
++
++	fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
++	if (fd &lt; 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "offline (socket)");
++		return;
++	}
++	flags = fcntl(fd, F_GETFL, 0);
++	if (flags &gt;= 0)
++		fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK);
++
++	memset(&amp;addr, 0, sizeof(addr));
++	addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
++	addr.sin_port = htons(53);
++	inet_pton(AF_INET, "1.1.1.1", &amp;addr.sin_addr);
++
++	gettimeofday(&amp;tv0, NULL);
++	if (connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&amp;addr, sizeof(addr)) &lt; 0 &amp;&amp;
++	    errno != EINPROGRESS) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "offline");
++		close(fd);
++		return;
++	}
++	FD_ZERO(&amp;wfds);
++	FD_SET(fd, &amp;wfds);
++	tv.tv_sec = 1;
++	tv.tv_usec = 500000;
++	if (select(fd + 1, NULL, &amp;wfds, NULL, &amp;tv) &lt;= 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "offline (timeout)");
++		close(fd);
++		return;
++	}
++	if (getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, &amp;err, &amp;elen) &lt; 0 || err != 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "offline");
++		close(fd);
++		return;
++	}
++	gettimeofday(&amp;tv1, NULL);
++	ms = (tv1.tv_sec - tv0.tv_sec) * 1000L +
++	     (tv1.tv_usec - tv0.tv_usec) / 1000L;
++	close(fd);
++	snprintf(out, n, "online  (~%ld ms to 1.1.1.1)", ms);
++}
++
++/* Minimal HTTP/1.0 GET (no TLS) — wttr.in format string. */
++static int http_get_plain(const char *host, const char *path, char *body,
++			  size_t body_len)
++{
++	struct addrinfo hints, *res = NULL, *rp;
++	int fd = -1, n;
++	char req[512], buf[2048];
++	size_t blen = 0;
++	char *hdr_end;
++
++	memset(&amp;hints, 0, sizeof(hints));
++	hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
++	hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC;
++	if (getaddrinfo(host, "80", &amp;hints, &amp;res) != 0)
++		return -1;
++	for (rp = res; rp; rp = rp-&gt;ai_next) {
++		fd = socket(rp-&gt;ai_family, rp-&gt;ai_socktype, rp-&gt;ai_protocol);
++		if (fd &lt; 0)
++			continue;
++		{
++			struct timeval tv = { .tv_sec = 3, .tv_usec = 0 };
++			setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &amp;tv, sizeof(tv));
++			setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, &amp;tv, sizeof(tv));
++		}
++		if (connect(fd, rp-&gt;ai_addr, rp-&gt;ai_addrlen) == 0)
++			break;
++		close(fd);
++		fd = -1;
++	}
++	freeaddrinfo(res);
++	if (fd &lt; 0)
++		return -1;
++
++	n = snprintf(req, sizeof(req),
++		     "GET %s HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: %s\r\nUser-Agent: bgtk-sys_status\r\n"
++		     "Connection: close\r\n\r\n",
++		     path, host);
++	if (write(fd, req, (size_t)n) &lt; 0) {
++		close(fd);
++		return -1;
++	}
++	while (blen + 1 &lt; sizeof(buf)) {
++		ssize_t r = read(fd, buf + blen, sizeof(buf) - 1 - blen);
++		if (r &lt;= 0)
++			break;
++		blen += (size_t)r;
++	}
++	close(fd);
++	buf[blen] = '\0';
++	hdr_end = strstr(buf, "\r\n\r\n");
++	if (!hdr_end)
++		return -1;
++	hdr_end += 4;
++	/* trim whitespace / newlines from weather line */
++	while (*hdr_end &amp;&amp; isspace((unsigned char)*hdr_end))
++		hdr_end++;
++	{
++		char *e = hdr_end + strlen(hdr_end);
++		while (e &gt; hdr_end &amp;&amp; isspace((unsigned char)e[-1]))
++			*--e = '\0';
++	}
++	if (!*hdr_end)
++		return -1;
++	snprintf(body, body_len, "%s", hdr_end);
++	return 0;
++}
++
++static void metric_weather(char *out, size_t n)
++{
++	char body[256];
++	char clean[256];
++	char *p, *q;
++	int sp = 0;
++
++	/* Location + temp only (ASCII). Avoid emoji — BGTK draws one byte per
++	 * FreeType index, so multi-byte UTF-8 looks like garbage. */
++	if (http_get_plain("wttr.in", "/?format=%l:+%t", body, sizeof(body)) != 0) {
++		snprintf(out, n, "n/a (network)");
++		return;
++	}
++	/* Keep printable ASCII; map other bytes to nothing (strip UTF-8). */
++	for (p = body, q = clean; *p &amp;&amp; (size_t)(q - clean) + 1 &lt; sizeof(clean); p++) {
++		unsigned char c = (unsigned char)*p;
++		if (c &gt;= 32 &amp;&amp; c &lt; 127) {
++			if (c == ' ') {
++				if (!sp) {
++					*q++ = ' ';
++					sp = 1;
++				}
++			} else {
++				*q++ = (char)c;
++				sp = 0;
++			}
++		}
++	}
++	*q = '\0';
++	if (!clean[0])
++		snprintf(out, n, "n/a");
++	else
++		snprintf(out, n, "%s", clean);
++}
++
++/* Refresh bitflags — different intervals in the main loop. */
++enum {
++	REFRESH_CLOCK = 1u &lt;&lt; 0,   /* 1s */
++	REFRESH_FAST = 1u &lt;&lt; 1,    /* 2s: uptime, cpu, mem, swap */
++	REFRESH_DISK = 1u &lt;&lt; 2,    /* 30s */
++	REFRESH_NET = 1u &lt;&lt; 3,     /* 30s */
++	REFRESH_WEATHER = 1u &lt;&lt; 4, /* 10 min */
++	REFRESH_ALL = 0x1fu
++};
++
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++/* Collect selected metrics + push into labels                         */
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++
++void sys_status_refresh(unsigned flags)
++{
++	char buf[160];
++
++	if (flags &amp; REFRESH_CLOCK) {
++		metric_clock(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_CLOCK])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_CLOCK], buf);
++	}
++	if (flags &amp; REFRESH_FAST) {
++		metric_uptime(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_UPTIME])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_UPTIME], buf);
++		metric_cpu(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_CPU])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_CPU], buf);
++		{
++			char swap[160];
++			metric_mem_swap(buf, sizeof(buf), swap, sizeof(swap));
++			if (value_labels[ROW_MEM])
++				set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_MEM], buf);
++			if (value_labels[ROW_SWAP])
++				set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_SWAP], swap);
++		}
++	}
++	if (flags &amp; REFRESH_DISK) {
++		metric_disk(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_DISK])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_DISK], buf);
++	}
++	if (flags &amp; REFRESH_NET) {
++		metric_internet(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_NET])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_NET], buf);
++	}
++	if (flags &amp; REFRESH_WEATHER) {
++		metric_weather(buf, sizeof(buf));
++		if (value_labels[ROW_WEATHER])
++			set_label_text(value_labels[ROW_WEATHER], buf);
++	}
++}
++
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++/* UI                                                                  */
++/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
++
++/* Size root frame from label text (call after metrics are filled). */
++static void sys_status_fit_size(struct BGTK_Context *c, struct BGTK_Widget *frame)
++{
++	int i, tw, th;
++	int name_w = 0, val_w = 0, text_h = 0;
++	int row_m = 1, row_p = 2;
++	int list_m = 4, list_p = 4;
++	int frame_p = 4, bw;
++	int row_w, row_h, list_w, list_h;
++
++	if (!c || !frame || !root_list)
++		return;
++
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; N_ROWS; i++) {
++		const char *ns = name_labels[i] &amp;&amp; name_labels[i]-&gt;data.text.text
++					 ? name_labels[i]-&gt;data.text.text
++					 : row_names[i];
++		const char *vs = value_labels[i] &amp;&amp; value_labels[i]-&gt;data.text.text
++					 ? value_labels[i]-&gt;data.text.text
++					 : "?";
++		int nh, vh;
++
++		measure_text(c-&gt;ft_face, ns, &amp;tw, &amp;th);
++		nh = th + 2 * (3 + 1); /* text padding=3 margin=1 */
++		tw += 2 * (3 + 1);
++		if (tw &gt; name_w)
++			name_w = tw;
++		if (nh &gt; text_h)
++			text_h = nh;
++
++		measure_text(c-&gt;ft_face, vs, &amp;tw, &amp;th);
++		vh = th + 2 * (3 + 1);
++		tw += 2 * (3 + 1);
++		if (tw &gt; val_w)
++			val_w = tw;
++		if (vh &gt; text_h)
++			text_h = vh;
++	}
++	/* A little slack so a slightly longer sample does not clip. */
++	name_w += 4;
++	val_w += 8;
++
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; N_ROWS; i++) {
++		if (name_labels[i]) {
++			name_labels[i]-&gt;w = name_w;
++			name_labels[i]-&gt;h = text_h;
++		}
++		if (value_labels[i]) {
++			value_labels[i]-&gt;w = val_w;
++			value_labels[i]-&gt;h = text_h;
++		}
++		/* horizontal list: content = sum(w) + 2*m*(n-1), plus pad/margin */
++		row_w = name_w + val_w + 2 * row_m + 2 * (row_p + row_m);
++		row_h = text_h + 2 * (row_p + row_m);
++		if (row_widgets[i]) {
++			row_widgets[i]-&gt;w = row_w;
++			row_widgets[i]-&gt;h = row_h;
++		}
++	}
++
++	/* vertical list of N rows */
++	list_w = row_w + 2 * (list_p + list_m);
++	list_h = N_ROWS * row_h + 2 * list_m * (N_ROWS - 1) +
++		 2 * (list_p + list_m);
++	root_list-&gt;w = list_w;
++	root_list-&gt;h = list_h;
++
++	bw = frame-&gt;data.frame.border_w;
++	if (bw &lt; 1)
++		bw = 1;
++	frame-&gt;w = list_w + 2 * (frame_p + bw);
++	frame-&gt;h = list_h + 2 * (frame_p + bw);
++	if (frame-&gt;w &lt; 1)
++		frame-&gt;w = 1;
++	if (frame-&gt;h &lt; 1)
++		frame-&gt;h = 1;
++}
++
++struct BGTK_Widget *sys_status_build_ui(struct BGTK_Context *c)
++{
++	struct BGTK_Widget *rows[N_ROWS];
++	struct BGTK_Widget *list, *frame;
++	int i;
++
++	ctx = c;
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; N_ROWS; i++) {
++		name_labels[i] = NULL;
++		value_labels[i] = NULL;
++		row_widgets[i] = NULL;
++	}
++	root_list = NULL;
++
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; N_ROWS; i++) {
++		struct BGTK_Widget *name =
++			bgtk_text(c, (char *)row_names[i],
++				  (BGTK_Options){.padding = 3, .margin = 1});
++		struct BGTK_Widget *val =
++			bgtk_text(c, "…",
++				  (BGTK_Options){.padding = 3, .margin = 1});
++		struct BGTK_Widget *pair[2] = { name, val };
++		struct BGTK_Widget *row;
++
++		name_labels[i] = name;
++		value_labels[i] = val;
++		row = bgtk_list(c, pair, 2,
++				(BGTK_Options){
++					.orientation = BGTK_LIST_HORIZONTAL,
++					.padding = 2,
++					.margin = 1,
++				});
++		row_widgets[i] = row;
++		rows[i] = row;
++	}
++
++	list = bgtk_list(c, rows, N_ROWS,
++			 (BGTK_Options){
++				 .orientation = BGTK_LIST_VERTICAL,
++				 .padding = 4,
++				 .margin = 4,
++			 });
++	root_list = list;
++	/* Temporary size; sys_status_fit_size sets the real one. */
++	frame = bgtk_frame(c, list, 1, 1,
++			   (BGTK_Options){.padding = 4, .margin = 0});
++
++	/* Prime CPU sample, then full fill (weather may block once). */
++	sys_status_refresh(REFRESH_ALL &amp; ~REFRESH_WEATHER);
++	sys_status_refresh(REFRESH_FAST | REFRESH_WEATHER);
++	sys_status_fit_size(c, frame);
++	return frame;
++}
++
++#ifndef SYS_STATUS_TEST_MODE
++
++/* Replace the mapped buffer with one of the measured size. */
++static int sys_status_apply_size(struct BGTK_Context *c, int conn, int w, int h)
++{
++	struct BufferRequest req;
++	void *nb;
++	size_t old_bytes;
++
++	if (!c || w &lt; 1 || h &lt; 1)
++		return -1;
++	if (w == c-&gt;width &amp;&amp; h == c-&gt;height)
++		return 0;
++
++	req.width = (uint32_t)w;
++	req.height = (uint32_t)h;
++	/* Same calling convention as other BGTK apps (by value). */
++	nb = bgce_get_buffer(conn, req);
++	if (!nb) {
++		bgtk_log("resize get_buffer %dx%d failed", w, h);
++		return -1;
++	}
++	old_bytes = (size_t)c-&gt;width * (size_t)c-&gt;height * BGCE_BPP;
++	if (c-&gt;shm_buffer) {
++		if (c-&gt;buffer_mapped &amp;&amp; old_bytes &gt; 0)
++			munmap(c-&gt;shm_buffer, old_bytes);
++		else
++			free(c-&gt;shm_buffer);
++	}
++	c-&gt;shm_buffer = nb;
++	c-&gt;buffer_mapped = 1;
++	c-&gt;width = w;
++	c-&gt;height = h;
++	if (c-&gt;root_widget) {
++		c-&gt;root_widget-&gt;w = c-&gt;width;
++		c-&gt;root_widget-&gt;h = c-&gt;height;
++	}
++	bgtk_log("window sized to %dx%d", c-&gt;width, c-&gt;height);
++	return 0;
++}
++
++int main(void)
++{
++	int conn;
++	struct BufferRequest req;
++	void *buf;
++	struct BGCEMessage msg;
++	struct timeval now, t_clock, t_fast, t_disk, t_weather;
++	int need_draw = 1;
++	struct BGTK_Widget *root;
++
++	bgtk_log_open("sys_status");
++	bgtk_log("starting system status");
++
++	conn = bgce_connect();
++	if (conn &lt; 0) {
++		bgtk_log_errno("bgce_connect");
++		return 1;
++	}
++	/* Bootstrap buffer so FreeType is available to measure labels. */
++	req.width = BOOT_W;
++	req.height = BOOT_H;
++	buf = bgce_get_buffer(conn, req);
++	if (!buf) {
++		bgtk_log("bgce_get_buffer failed");
++		bgce_disconnect(conn);
++		return 1;
++	}
++	ctx = bgtk_init(conn, buf, BOOT_W, BOOT_H);
++	if (!ctx) {
++		bgtk_log("bgtk_init failed");
++		bgce_disconnect(conn);
++		return 1;
++	}
++
++	root = sys_status_build_ui(ctx);
++	ctx-&gt;root_widget = root;
++	/* Request the measured content size (tight fit). */
++	if (sys_status_apply_size(ctx, conn, root-&gt;w, root-&gt;h) != 0)
++		bgtk_log("keeping bootstrap size %dx%d", ctx-&gt;width, ctx-&gt;height);
++
++	gettimeofday(&amp;now, NULL);
++	t_clock = t_fast = t_disk = t_weather = now;
++	bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++
++	/* Poll; refresh groups on their own intervals (not everything at 1s). */
++	for (;;) {
++		fd_set rfds;
++		struct timeval tv;
++		int r;
++		unsigned flags = 0;
++		long ms_clock, ms_fast, ms_disk, ms_weather;
++
++		FD_ZERO(&amp;rfds);
++		FD_SET(conn, &amp;rfds);
++		tv.tv_sec = 0;
++		tv.tv_usec = 200000; /* 200ms */
++		r = select(conn + 1, &amp;rfds, NULL, NULL, &amp;tv);
++		if (r &lt; 0) {
++			if (errno == EINTR)
++				continue;
++			bgtk_log_errno("select");
++			break;
++		}
++		if (r &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; FD_ISSET(conn, &amp;rfds)) {
++			ssize_t n = bgce_recv_msg(conn, &amp;msg);
++			if (n &lt;= 0) {
++				bgtk_log("connection closed");
++				break;
++			}
++			if (msg.type == MSG_INPUT_EVENT) {
++				struct InputEvent *ev = &amp;msg.data.input_event;
++				if (ev-&gt;type == EV_REL || ev-&gt;type == EV_ABS)
++					continue;
++				bgtk_update_modifiers(ctx, *ev);
++				if (bgtk_is_app_quit_event(ctx, *ev))
++					break;
++				if (bgtk_handle_input_event(ctx, *ev))
++					need_draw = 1;
++			} else if (msg.type == MSG_FOCUS_CHANGE) {
++				bgtk_set_window_focus(ctx,
++						      msg.data.focus_event.state);
++			} else if (msg.type == MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE) {
++				if (bgtk_handle_buffer_change(
++					    ctx, &amp;msg.data.buffer_reply) == 0) {
++					if (ctx-&gt;root_widget) {
++						ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;w = ctx-&gt;width;
++						ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;h = ctx-&gt;height;
++					}
++					need_draw = 1;
++				}
++			}
++		}
++
++		gettimeofday(&amp;now, NULL);
++#define MS_SINCE(t0) \
++	((now.tv_sec - (t0).tv_sec) * 1000L + \
++	 (now.tv_usec - (t0).tv_usec) / 1000L)
++		ms_clock = MS_SINCE(t_clock);
++		ms_fast = MS_SINCE(t_fast);
++		ms_disk = MS_SINCE(t_disk);
++		ms_weather = MS_SINCE(t_weather);
++#undef MS_SINCE
++		if (ms_clock &gt;= 1000) {
++			flags |= REFRESH_CLOCK;
++			t_clock = now;
++		}
++		if (ms_fast &gt;= 2000) {
++			flags |= REFRESH_FAST;
++			t_fast = now;
++		}
++		if (ms_disk &gt;= 30000) {
++			flags |= REFRESH_DISK | REFRESH_NET;
++			t_disk = now;
++		}
++		if (ms_weather &gt;= 600000) {
++			flags |= REFRESH_WEATHER;
++			t_weather = now;
++		}
++		if (flags) {
++			sys_status_refresh(flags);
++			need_draw = 1;
++		}
++		if (need_draw) {
++			bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++			need_draw = 0;
++		}
++	}
++
++	bgtk_destroy(ctx);
++	bgce_disconnect(conn);
++	return 0;
++}

+parent <a href=commit-26ab185.html>26ab185</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-06T15:43:48-03:00
+
+    fix: redraw after window resize instead of a black frame.
+
+    BGCE sends MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE with a new shm mapping on resize; apps
+    were ignoring it and kept the old buffer. Add bgtk_handle_buffer_change
+    to remount the framebuffer, reflow the launcher layout, and redraw.
+    Wire the same path into other BGCE apps and cover resize in headless.
+
+<a href=tree-8f0bef5.html>tree</a>
+

+ 			bgtk_set_window_focus(ctx, msg.data.focus_event.state);
+ 			break;
+ 		case MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE:
++			if (bgtk_handle_buffer_change(ctx, &amp;msg.data.buffer_reply) == 0) {
++				if (ctx-&gt;root_widget) {
++					ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;w = ctx-&gt;width;
++					ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;h = ctx-&gt;height;
++				}
++				bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++			}
+ 			break;
+ 		default:
+ 			break;

+ 			case MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE:
++				if (bgtk_handle_buffer_change(ctx, &amp;msg.data.buffer_reply) == 0) {
++					if (ctx-&gt;root_widget) {
++						ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;w = ctx-&gt;width;
++						ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;h = ctx-&gt;height;
++					}
++					bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++					res = 0;
++				}
+ 				break;
+ 			default:
+ 				break;

++	if (inner_w &lt; 40)
++		inner_w = 40;
++	if (inner_h &lt; 40)
++		inner_h = 40;
++
++	if (text_input) {
++		text_input-&gt;w = inner_w;
++		/* height stays content-sized; force a sensible min */
++		if (text_input-&gt;h &lt; 28)
++			text_input-&gt;h = 28;
++	}
++	if (matches_scroll) {
++		int input_h = text_input ? text_input-&gt;h + 8 : 36;
++		matches_scroll-&gt;w = inner_w;
++		matches_scroll-&gt;h = inner_h - input_h;
++		if (matches_scroll-&gt;h &lt; 40)
++			matches_scroll-&gt;h = 40;
++	}
++	if (ctx-&gt;root_widget) {
++		ctx-&gt;root_widget-&gt;w = ctx-&gt;width;

+-# BGTK (Brian's Graphical Toolkit)
++# BGTK - Brian's GUI Toolkit - Agent Guide
++
++## Project Overview
++
++BGTK (Brian's GUI Toolkit) is a lightweight GUI toolkit designed for Linux systems. It provides a set of widgets and a rendering system for building graphical user interfaces.
++
++## Codebase Structure
++
++```
++/
++├── AGENTS.md         - This file, guidance for agents working on the project
++├── app.c             - Test application entry point
++├── bgtk.c            - Core BGTK implementation
++├── bgtk.h            - Public API headers
++├── config.c          - Configuration file parsing
++├── config.h          - Configuration definitions
++├── drawing.c         - Drawing and rendering functions
++├── internal.h        - Internal headers and definitions
++├── Makefile          - Build configuration
++├── README.md         - Project overview
++├── stb_image.h       - STB image loading library
++├── stb_image_write.h - STB image writing library
++├── test/             - Test scripts and utilities
++└── widgets.c         - Widget implementations
++```
++
++## Key Components
++
++### 1. BGTK Context (`struct BGTK_Context`)
++- Central structure holding application state
++- Manages the connection to the display server
++- Contains the root widget and focused widget
++- Handles theme and font information
++
++### 2. Widget System
++- Base widget structure: `struct BGTK_Widget`
++- Widget types: Button, Label, Text, Scrollable, Image, Frame, TextInput
++- Each widget has:
++  - Position and dimensions (x, y, w, h)
++  - Styling properties (padding, margin, flags)
++  - Type-specific data in a union
++  - Event handling function (`handle_event`)
++
++### 3. Event Handling
++- Events start at the root widget and propagate down to children
++- Each widget can handle or pass through events
++- Mouse and keyboard events are supported
++- Focus management for text input
++
++### 4. Drawing System
++- Widgets are drawn to a shared memory buffer
++- Drawing functions in `drawing.c`
++- Supports text rendering with FreeType
++- Handles widget layout and positioning
++
++## Development Guidelines
++
++### Coding Style
++- Follow existing code style (indentation, naming, etc.)
++- Use clear, descriptive variable and function names
++- Keep functions focused on single responsibilities
++- Add comments for complex logic
++
++### Widget Implementation
++1. Add new widget type to `enum BGTK_Widget_Type`
++2. Add widget-specific data to the union in `struct BGTK_Widget`
++3. Implement creation function in `widgets.c`
++4. Implement drawing logic in `drawing.c`
++5. Implement event handler (or use default)
++6. Add declaration to `bgtk.h`
++
++### Event Handling
++- Each widget should implement `handle_event`
++- Return 1 if event is handled, 0 otherwise
++- For container widgets, propagate events to children
++- Transform event coordinates for child widgets
++
++## Common Tasks
++
++### Adding a New Widget
++1. Define the widget data structure in the union
++2. Create a constructor function in `widgets.c`
++3. Implement the drawing function in `drawing.c`
++4. Implement event handling if needed
++5. Add the constructor to `bgtk.h`
++
++### Modifying Event Handling
++1. Update widget-specific handlers in `widgets.c`
++2. Modify `bgtk_handle_input_event` in `bgtk.c` if needed
++3. Ensure proper event propagation
++
++### Adding New Features
++1. Add necessary data structures
++2. Implement core functionality
++3. Add configuration options if needed
++4. Update documentation
++
++## Testing
++
++### Manual Testing
++- Run the application and interact with widgets
++- Test edge cases (rapid clicks, keyboard input, etc.)
++- Verify visual appearance
++
++### Automated Testing
++- Test scripts are in the `test/` directory
++- Run with `./test/server_client.sh`
++
++### Debugging Tips
++- Use `printf` for debugging output
++- Check widget bounds and positions
++- Verify event coordinates
++
++## Important Notes for Agents
++
++1. **Event Coordinate System**: Events use absolute screen coordinates. When propagating to children, transform coordinates to be relative to the child widget.
++
++2. **Widget Hierarchy**: The root widget is in `ctx-&gt;root_widget`. Child widgets are stored in parent widgets.
++
++3. **Focus Management**: Text input widgets need special handling for keyboard events. Use `bgtk_set_focus()` to manage focus.
++
++4. **Drawing**: Widgets are drawn to `ctx-&gt;shm_buffer`. Use the drawing functions in `drawing.c`.
++
++5. **Memory Management**: Widgets are responsible for freeing their own resources in the destructor.
++
++6. **Configuration**: Theme and font settings are loaded from a config file at startup.
++
++## Useful Functions
++
++- `bgtk_init()`: Initialize the BGTK context
++- `bgtk_destroy()`: Clean up resources
++- `bgtk_handle_input_event()`: Handle input events
++- `bgtk_draw_widgets()`: Render all widgets
++- `bgtk_set_focus()`: Set the focused widget
++- `draw_widget()`: Draw a single widget
++- `calculate_widget_size()`: Calculate widget dimensions and positions
+ 
+ This is a toolkit for the BGCE display server. It works by directly writing to
+ a graphical buffer, this library lets developers create user interfaces easily.
+ 
+-
+-## Style guide
+-
+-Prefer passing struct pointers to functions instead of malloc'ing them in the function:
+-
+-struct ctx = ...
+-int res = bgtk_init(&amp;ctx);
+-
+-
+-## Roadmap
+-
+-[ ] **Step 1: Define BGTK Interface (`bgtk.h`)**
+-    * Define the core structure for a widget (`struct BGTK_Widget`).
+-    * Define the event structure (`struct BGTK_Event`).
+-    [ ] Improve widget structure: add options (like alignment), child widgets.
+-    [ ] Add methods to update a widget's property so it redraws automaticaly.
+-
+-[ ] **Step 2: Implement BGTK Core (`bgtk.c`)**
+-    [X] Implement initialization, event queueing, and simple drawing (e.g., drawing rectangles for buttons, text rendering).
+-    [X] Only call draw when changes are made, like input.
+-    [ ] Implement proper hit detection: using widget trees and coordinates, e.g. click on x,y -&gt; search the tree until last widget is found, then send the input to that widget.
+-        [ ] Implement this approach: each widget has a handle_event() function and if hit runs the function. Also set the focus.
+-            [ ] Scrollable will find which item got the event and call the event handler of the item
+-            [ ] Frame will pass to the child
+-            [ ] Button calls the button handler
+-            [ ] Input text sets the input focus 
+-    [X] Add support for screenshots
+-    [ ] Add a generic scroll widget, that scrolls content
+-        [ ] Add options for vertical or horizontal
+-    [X] Add a image widget that supports image files:
+-        [X] png
+-        [X] svg
+-        [X] jpeg
+-
+-[x] **Step 3: Integrate and Test**
+-    [X] Create a new client file (or update `client.c`) to demonstrate a basic BGTK application. -&gt; app.c
+-
+-
+-## Useful Hints for Agents
+-
+-- The project uses **absolute positioning** for widgets. Future work includes adding
+-  layout managers (e.g., box, grid).
+-- **FreeType** is used for font rendering. Ensure the font path in `bgtk.c` is valid
+-  or make it configurable.
+-- **BGCE** is the display server. The connection is established in `bgtk_init()`.
+-- **Event handling** is done in `bgtk_main_loop()`. It currently processes input events
+-  and redraws the screen.
+-- **Widget updates**: When a widget's property changes (e.g., label text), it should
+-  trigger a redraw. This is partially implemented.
+-- **Code style**: Use the provided `.clang-format` file. Key rules:
+-  - Braces on the same line for `if`, `for`, `while`, etc.
+-  - Never omit braces for single-line blocks.
+-  - If function arguments don't fit on one line, place each on a new line and close
+-    the parenthesis on its own line.
+-- **Testing**: The `app.c` file is a demo application. Use it to test new features.
+-
+-
+-### Adding new widgets
+-
+-1. Updated bgtk.h to add the type in the enum and in the union
+-2. Update widgets.c to add a function to create it
+-2. Update drawing.c to update the draw_widget function

+-		// TODO: descend to the last scrollable widget

+-	// Only handle mouse button presses for now

+-
+-	// Handle mouse clicks (set focus or trigger callbacks)
+-	if (ev.code == BTN_LEFT &amp;&amp; ev.value == 1) {
+-		printf("BGTK Got click: (%d, %d)\n", ev.x, ev.y);
+-		// Traverse widgets to find the clicked widget
+-		struct BGTK_Widget* w = ctx-&gt;root_widget;
+-		struct BGTK_Widget* clicked_widget = NULL;

+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-09T17:12:28-03:00
+
+    feat: layout expand/relative, settings reflow, gemini ereandel keys
+
+    Add FILL/EXPAND/RELATIVE layout helpers and wire settings shell through
+    them. Gemini browser gains ereandel-style history and keys (b/u/o/r/…),
+    sturdier shortcut handling, and roomier gemtext spacing. Widen switch
+    tracks.
+
+<a href=tree-91eaa64.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/AGENTS.md b/AGENTS.md
+index 81aadea..1954869 100644
+--- a/AGENTS.md
++++ b/AGENTS.md
+@@ -235,13 +235,19 @@ etc.) still need BGCE on Linux.
+ 
+ ## Important Notes for Agents
+ 
+-1. **Event Coordinate System**: Events use absolute screen coordinates. When propagating to children, transform coordinates to be relative to the child widget.
+-2. **Widget Hierarchy**: The root widget is in `ctx-&gt;root_widget`. Child widgets are stored in parent widgets.
++1. **Event Coordinate System**: Pointer events use screen coordinates at the root.
++   Hit-test with `bgtk_widget_hit()` (handles `BGTK_FLAG_RELATIVE`). Scrollables
++   still transform events into content space for their children.
++2. **Widget Hierarchy**: Root is `ctx-&gt;root_widget`. Containers set `child-&gt;parent`.
+ 3. **Focus Management**: Text input widgets need special handling for keyboard events. Use `bgtk_set_focus()` to manage focus.
+ 4. **Drawing**: Widgets are drawn to `ctx-&gt;shm_buffer`. Use the drawing functions in `drawing.c`.
+ 5. **Memory Management**: Widgets are responsible for freeing their own resources in the destructor. Mock contexts are freed with `bgtk_destroy_mock()`, real ones with `bgtk_destroy()`.
+ 6. **Configuration**: Theme and font settings are loaded from a config file at startup.
+ 7. **Platform**: Full BGCE apps are Linux-oriented. Headless/mock builds are the default on macOS (`Makefile` sets `TARGET = headless test_terminal test_html` on Darwin).
++8. **Layout flags** (optional; default is legacy absolute placement):
++   - `BGTK_FLAG_EXPAND_X` / `BGTK_FLAG_EXPAND_Y` / `BGTK_FLAG_FILL` — grow into free space in a parent list (main axis shared among expanders; cross axis fills content box). Parent list needs a fixed/pre-set size larger than content (e.g. filled by a frame).
++   - `BGTK_FLAG_RELATIVE` — `x`/`y` are parent-relative; `abs_x`/`abs_y` are screen (or scroll content) coords after layout. Set on a container to opt a subtree in; children inherit during place.
++   - `bgtk_widget_screen_pos()`, `bgtk_widget_hit()`, `bgtk_widget_set_parent()`.
+ 
+ ## Useful Functions
+ 
+@@ -254,6 +260,7 @@ etc.) still need BGCE on Linux.
+ - `take_screenshot()`: Write framebuffer to PNG
+ - `draw_widget()`: Draw a single widget
+ - `calculate_widget_size()`: Calculate widget dimensions and positions
++- `bgtk_widget_screen_pos()` / `bgtk_widget_hit()`: Screen bounds after layout
+ 
+ ### Widget constructors
+ - `bgtk_text()`, `bgtk_label()`, `bgtk_button()`, `bgtk_scrollable()`,

++static void bookmark_goto_page(void)

++			nl = strchr(line, '\n');

++					ul = sizeof(url) - 1;
++				memcpy(url, line, ul);

++				snprintf(entry, sizeof(entry), "=&gt; %s %s\n", url,
++					 sp + 1);
++			} else {
++				snprintf(entry, sizeof(entry), "=&gt; %s\n", line);
++			}
++			el = strlen(entry);

++				char *nb = realloc(body, len + el + 256);
++				if (!nb)
++					break;
++				body = nb;
++				cap = len + el + 256;
++			}
++			memcpy(body + len, entry, el + 1);
++			len += el;
++			n++;
++		}
++		fclose(f);
++	}
++	if (n == 0) {
++		const char *empty = "No bookmarks yet. Press m to add.\n";
++		size_t el = strlen(empty);
++		char *nb = realloc(body, len + el + 1);
++		if (nb) {
++			body = nb;
++			memcpy(body + len, empty, el + 1);
++		}
++	}
++	if (current_url[0])
++		hist_push(current_url);
++	free(last_body);
++	last_body = body;
++	snprintf(current_url, sizeof(current_url), "about:bookmarks");

++			(uint32_t)strlen(current_url);
++		addr_input-&gt;data.text_input.scroll_x = 0;
++	}
++	rebuild_content_from_gemtext(last_body);
++	if (content_scroll)
++		bgtk_set_focus(ctx, content_scroll);
++	else
++		bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++}

++{

+-## Themes
+-Theme config files allow customizing the appearance of BGTK applications.
+-To use a theme:
+-1. Create a config file in `~/.config/bgtk.conf`.
+-2. Define theme properties like colors and fonts in key-value pairs:
+-
+-```
+-background_color = #282828
+-text_color = #ebdbb2
+-font = /opt/fonts/.../DejaVu Sans.otf
++## Configuration
++
++BGTK is configured via `~/.config/bgtk.conf`. Example with all options and their defaults:
++
++```ini
++# Background settings
++[background]
++type = color
++color = #AAAAAA
++# Or use an image:
++# type = image
++# path = /path/to/wallpaper.png
++# mode = tiled
++
++# Theme colors and border sizes
++[theme]
++background = #AAAAAA
++button = #888888
++button_text = #000000
++button_border_size = 1
++input_border_size = 1
++frame_border_size = 4
++frame_border_color = #FFFFFF
++
++# Font settings
++[font]
++path = /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf
++size = 12
+ ```
+ 
++Colors use `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` format. Lines starting with `#` or `;` are comments.
++
+ 
+ ## Building
+

++# BGTK (Brian's Graphical Toolkit)
++
++This is a toolkit for the BGCE display server. It works by directly writing to
++a graphical buffer, this library lets developers create user interfaces easily.
++
++
++## Roadmap
++
++[ ] **Step 1: Define BGTK Interface (`bgtk.h`)**
++    * Define the core structure for a widget (`struct BGTK_Widget`).
++    * Define the event structure (`struct BGTK_Event`).
++    [ ] Improve widget structure: add options (like alignment), child widgets.
++    [ ] Add methods to update a widget's property so it redraws automaticaly.
++    * Define API functions:
++        * `BGTK_Context *bgtk_init(void)`: Connects to BGCE server, gets buffer/dimensions.
++        * `void bgtk_main_loop(BGTK_Context *ctx)`: Blocking loop to handle events and redraws.
++        * `BGTK_Widget *bgtk_label_new(const char *text)`: Creates a label.
++        * `BGTK_Widget *bgtk_button_new(const char *text, void (*callback)(void))`
++        * `void bgtk_add_widget(BGTK_Context *ctx, BGTK_Widget *widget, int x, int y, int w, int h)`: Simple absolute positioning for now.
++
++[ ] **Step 2: Implement BGTK Core (`bgtk.c`)**
++    [X] Implement initialization, event queueing, and simple drawing (e.g., drawing rectangles for buttons, text rendering).
++    [ ] Only call draw when changes are made, like input.
++    [ ] Implement proper hit detection: using widget trees and coordinates, e.g. click on x,y -&gt; search the tree until last widget is found, then send the input to that widget.
++    [ ] Add a generic scroll widget, that scrolls content

++
++## Useful Hints for Agents
++
++- The project uses **absolute positioning** for widgets. Future work includes adding
++  layout managers (e.g., box, grid).
++- **FreeType** is used for font rendering. Ensure the font path in `bgtk.c` is valid
++  or make it configurable.
++- **BGCE** is the display server. The connection is established in `bgtk_init()`.
++- **Event handling** is done in `bgtk_main_loop()`. It currently processes input events
++  and redraws the screen.
++- **Widget updates**: When a widget's property changes (e.g., label text), it should
++  trigger a redraw. This is partially implemented.
++- **Code style**: Use the provided `.clang-format` file. Key rules:
++  - Braces on the same line for `if`, `for`, `while`, etc.
++  - Never omit braces for single-line blocks.
++  - If function arguments don't fit on one line, place each on a new line and close
++    the parenthesis on its own line.
++- **Testing**: The `app.c` file is a demo application. Use it to test new features.

++# Makefile for BGTK
++
++CFLAGS = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I. -I/usr/include/freetype2 -I/usr/local/include/bgce
++LDFLAGS = -lfreetype -lbgce
++
++TARGET = app
++SRC = app.c bgtk.c
++OBJ = $(SRC:.c=.o)
++
++.PHONY: all clean test
++
++all: $(TARGET)
++
++$(TARGET): $(OBJ)
++	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)
++
++%.o: %.c
++	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $&lt;
++
++clean:
++	rm -f $(TARGET) $(OBJ)
++
++test: $(TARGET)
++
++.PHONY: test
++	@echo "Starting BGCE server in background..."
++	bgce &amp;
++	BGCE_PID=$$
++	@echo "Running $(TARGET)..."
++	./$(TARGET) || true
++	@echo "Killing BGCE server (PID: $$BGCE_PID)..."
++	kill $$BGCE_PID 2&gt;/dev/null || true
++	@echo "Test complete."

++# BGTK (Brian's Graphical Toolkit)
++
++A lightweight toolkit for the BGCE display server. This library allows developers to
++create graphical user interfaces by directly writing to a shared graphical buffer.
++
++## Features
++- Simple widget system (labels, buttons).
++- Direct rendering to a shared memory buffer.
++- Event handling for user input.
++- Basic font rendering using FreeType.
++
++## Building
++
++Requirements:
++- A C compiler (GCC or Clang).
++- FreeType development libraries.
++- BGCE server running.
++
++```sh
++make
++```
++
++## Running
++
++Start the BGCE server, then run the demo application:
++
++```sh
++./app
++```
++
++## Project Structure
++- `bgtk.h`: Public API and type definitions.
++- `bgtk.c`: Core implementation.
++- `app.c`: Demo application.
++- `Makefile`: Build system.
++- `.clang-format`: Code style configuration.
++
+diff --git a/app.c b/app.c
+new file mode 100644

+--- /dev/null
++++ b/app.c
+@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
++#include "bgtk.h"
++#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
++#include &lt;string.h&gt;
++
++static int counter = 0;
++static BGTK_Widget* counter_label = NULL;
++BGTK_Context* ctx = NULL;
++
++void button_callback(void) {
++	counter++;
++	printf("Button clicked! Counter: %d\n", counter);
++
++	if (counter_label &amp;&amp; counter_label-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL) {
++		puts(" setting new label");
++		char counter_text[32];
++		sprintf(counter_text, "Counter: %d", counter);
++		printf("calling set_label: %p\n", counter_label-&gt;set_label);
++		counter_label-&gt;set_label(counter_label, counter_text);
++		// Note: Widget size should ideally be recalculated here for layout purposes,
++		// but for absolute layout, we omit it for now.
++	}
++}
++
++int main(void) {
++	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0); // Disable buffering for stdout
++	setvbuf(stderr, NULL, _IONBF, 0); // Disable buffering for stderr
++
++	ctx = bgtk_init();
++	if (!ctx) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize BGTK.\n");
++		return 1;
++	}
++	printf("BGTK init done\n");
++
++	// 1. Create Widgets
++	char* counter_text = "Counter: 0";
++
++	BGTK_Widget* title = bgtk_label_new(ctx, "BGTK Demo Application");
++	BGTK_Widget* button = bgtk_button_new(ctx, "Click Me!", button_callback);
++	counter_label = bgtk_label_new(ctx, counter_text);
++	printf("BGTK added widgets\n");
++
++	// 2. Add Widgets (Absolute Positioning)
++	// Title at the top center
++	bgtk_add_widget(ctx, title, (ctx-&gt;width / 2) - (title-&gt;w / 2), 50, 0, 0);
++
++	// Button below the title
++	bgtk_add_widget(ctx, button, (ctx-&gt;width / 2) - (button-&gt;w / 2), 100, 0, 0);
++
++	// Label below the button
++	bgtk_add_widget(ctx, counter_label, (ctx-&gt;width / 2) - (counter_label-&gt;w / 2), 150, 0, 0);
++
++	printf("Starting BGTK main loop (%dx%d)...\n", ctx-&gt;width, ctx-&gt;height);
++	bgtk_main_loop(ctx);
++
++	bgtk_destroy(ctx);
++	return 0;
++}
+diff --git a/bgtk.c b/bgtk.c
+new file mode 100644
+index 0000000..85d92f2
+--- /dev/null
++++ b/bgtk.c
+@@ -0,0 +1,480 @@
++#include "bgtk.h"
++#include &lt;bgce.h&gt;
++
++#include &lt;errno.h&gt;
++#include &lt;linux/input.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
++#include &lt;string.h&gt;
++#include &lt;unistd.h&gt;
++
++// The font path is hardcoded for simplicity.
++#define DEFAULT_FONT_PATH "/usr/share/fonts/ttf-input/InputMono/InputMono/InputMono-Regular.ttf"
++#define DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE 12
++
++// Helper to create a generic widget
++static BGTK_Widget* bgtk_widget_new(BGTK_Context* ctx, BGTK_Widget_Type type) {
++	BGTK_Widget* widget = (BGTK_Widget*)calloc(1, sizeof(BGTK_Widget));
++	if (!widget) {
++		perror("calloc");
++		return NULL;
++	}
++	widget-&gt;ctx = ctx;
++	widget-&gt;type = type;
++	return widget;
++}
++
++// --- Core Functions ---
++
++BGTK_Context* bgtk_init(void) {
++	BGTK_Context* ctx = (BGTK_Context*)calloc(1, sizeof(BGTK_Context));
++	if (!ctx) {
++		perror("calloc");
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	ctx-&gt;conn_fd = -1; // Initialize fd to invalid value
++	ctx-&gt;font_size = DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE;
++
++	// 1. Initialize FreeType
++	if (FT_Init_FreeType(&amp;ctx-&gt;ft_library)) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_init: Could not init FreeType library.\n");
++		free(ctx);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	// 2. Load Font
++	if (FT_New_Face(ctx-&gt;ft_library, DEFAULT_FONT_PATH, 0, &amp;ctx-&gt;ft_face)) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_init: Could not load font %s. Falling back to simple drawing.\n", DEFAULT_FONT_PATH);
++		// Continue with default font context, simple text drawing is used later.
++	} else {
++		// Set font size
++		FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes(ctx-&gt;ft_face, 0, ctx-&gt;font_size);
++	}
++
++	// 3. Connect to BGCE
++	int conn_fd = bgce_connect();
++	if (conn_fd &lt; 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_init: Failed to connect to BGCE server.\n");
++		if (ctx-&gt;ft_library)
++			FT_Done_FreeType(ctx-&gt;ft_library);
++		free(ctx);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	// 4. Get Server Info (optional, but good for context)
++	struct ServerInfo s_info;
++	if (bgce_get_server_info(conn_fd, &amp;s_info) != 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_init: Failed to get server info.\n");
++		bgce_disconnect(conn_fd);
++		if (ctx-&gt;ft_library)
++			FT_Done_FreeType(ctx-&gt;ft_library);
++		free(ctx);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	//// 5. Subscribe to Input Events
++	// struct BGCEMessage sub_msg = { .type = MSG_SUBSCRIBE_INPUT };
++	//// This message has no payload, just the type.
++	// if (bgce_send_msg(conn_fd, &amp;sub_msg) &lt; 0) {
++	//     perror("bgtk_init: Failed to subscribe to input");
++	//     // Not fatal, but input won't work
++	// }
++
++	// 6. Request a buffer with server dimensions (full screen)
++	struct BufferRequest req = {
++	        .width = 600,
++	        .height = 480};
++
++	// We expect the libbgce function to handle the shm attach
++	void* buffer = bgce_get_buffer(conn_fd, req);
++	if (!buffer) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_init: Failed to get buffer from server.\n");
++		bgce_disconnect(conn_fd);
++		if (ctx-&gt;ft_library)
++			FT_Done_FreeType(ctx-&gt;ft_library);
++		free(ctx);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	ctx-&gt;conn_fd = conn_fd;
++	ctx-&gt;shm_buffer = buffer;
++	ctx-&gt;buf_width = 600;
++	ctx-&gt;buf_height = 480;
++
++	ctx-&gt;width = 600;
++	ctx-&gt;height = 480;
++
++	// Initial allocation for widgets
++	ctx-&gt;widget_capacity = 10;
++	ctx-&gt;widgets = (BGTK_Widget**)calloc(ctx-&gt;widget_capacity, sizeof(BGTK_Widget*));
++	if (!ctx-&gt;widgets) {
++		perror("calloc");
++		// Cleanup shm_buffer and FT
++		bgce_disconnect(conn_fd);
++		if (ctx-&gt;ft_library)
++			FT_Done_FreeType(ctx-&gt;ft_library);
++		free(ctx);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	return ctx;
++}
++
++void bgtk_destroy(BGTK_Context* ctx) {
++	if (!ctx)
++		return;
++
++	// Free all widgets
++	for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; ctx-&gt;widget_count; i++) {
++		BGTK_Widget* w = ctx-&gt;widgets[i];
++		if (w-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL) {
++			free(w-&gt;data.label.text);
++		} else if (w-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_BUTTON) {
++			free(w-&gt;data.button.text);
++		}
++		free(w);
++	}
++	free(ctx-&gt;widgets);
++
++	// Free FreeType resources
++	if (ctx-&gt;ft_face) {
++		FT_Done_Face(ctx-&gt;ft_face);
++	}
++	if (ctx-&gt;ft_library) {
++		FT_Done_FreeType(ctx-&gt;ft_library);
++	}
++
++	// Disconnect from BGCE
++	if (ctx-&gt;conn_fd &gt; 0) {
++		bgce_disconnect(ctx-&gt;conn_fd);
++	}
++
++	free(ctx);
++}
++
++// --- Drawing Primitives &amp; Widgets ---
++
++// A few basic colors (0xAARRGGBB)
++#define BGTK_COLOR_BG 0xFFCCCCCC    // Light Gray
++#define BGTK_COLOR_BTN 0xFF007BFF   // Blue
++#define BGTK_COLOR_TEXT 0xFF000000  // Black
++#define BGTK_COLOR_WHITE 0xFFFFFFFF // White
++
++static void bgtk_clear_buffer(BGTK_Context* ctx, uint32_t color) {
++	uint32_t* pixels = (uint32_t*)ctx-&gt;shm_buffer;
++	size_t size = (size_t)ctx-&gt;buf_width * ctx-&gt;buf_height;
++	for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) {
++		pixels[i] = color;
++	}
++}
++
++static void bgtk_draw_rect(BGTK_Context* ctx, int x, int y, int w, int h, uint32_t color) {
++	// Basic clipping and drawing
++	int x1 = x;
++	int y1 = y;
++	int x2 = x + w;
++	int y2 = y + h;
++
++	// Clip to buffer bounds
++	if (x1 &lt; 0)
++		x1 = 0;
++	if (y1 &lt; 0)
++		y1 = 0;
++	if (x2 &gt; (int)ctx-&gt;buf_width)
++		x2 = ctx-&gt;buf_width;
++	if (y2 &gt; (int)ctx-&gt;buf_height)
++		y2 = ctx-&gt;buf_height;
++
++	uint32_t* pixels = (uint32_t*)ctx-&gt;shm_buffer;
++	int stride = ctx-&gt;buf_width;
++
++	for (int j = y1; j &lt; y2; j++) {
++		for (int i = x1; i &lt; x2; i++) {
++			pixels[j * stride + i] = color;
++		}
++	}
++}
++
++void measure_text(FT_Face face, const char* text,
++                  int* out_width, int* out_height) {
++	int width = 0;
++
++	for (const char* p = text; *p; p++) {
++		if (FT_Load_Char(face, *p, FT_LOAD_DEFAULT))
++			continue;
++
++		width += face-&gt;glyph-&gt;advance.x; // 26.6 units
++	}
++
++	width &gt;&gt;= 6;
++
++	int ascent = face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.ascender &gt;&gt; 6;
++	int descent = -face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.descender &gt;&gt; 6;
++	int height = ascent + descent;
++
++	*out_width = width;
++	*out_height = height;
++}
++
++static void bgtk_draw_text(BGTK_Context* ctx, const char* text, int x, int y, uint32_t color) {
++	if (!ctx-&gt;ft_face) {
++		// Fallback to simple placeholder if font didn't load
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, x, y, 5, 5, color);
++		return;
++	}
++
++	// Set font size for drawing context
++	FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes(ctx-&gt;ft_face, 0, ctx-&gt;font_size);
++
++	int pen_x = x;
++	int pen_y = y + (ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.ascender &gt;&gt; 6);
++
++	uint32_t* pixels = ctx-&gt;shm_buffer;
++	int stride = ctx-&gt;buf_width;
++
++	for (const char* p = text; *p; p++) {
++		FT_UInt index = FT_Get_Char_Index(ctx-&gt;ft_face, *p);
++
++		if (FT_Load_Glyph(ctx-&gt;ft_face, index, FT_LOAD_DEFAULT | FT_LOAD_TARGET_LIGHT))
++			continue;
++
++		FT_Render_Glyph(ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;glyph, FT_RENDER_MODE_NORMAL);
++
++		FT_GlyphSlot slot = ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;glyph;
++		FT_Bitmap* bitmap = &amp;slot-&gt;bitmap;
++
++		int gx = pen_x + slot-&gt;bitmap_left;
++		int gy = pen_y - slot-&gt;bitmap_top;
++
++                for (unsigned int row = 0; row &lt; bitmap-&gt;rows; row++) {
++                        for (unsigned int col = 0; col &lt; bitmap-&gt;width; col++) {
++				uint8_t a = bitmap-&gt;buffer[row * bitmap-&gt;pitch + col];
++				if (a == 0)
++					continue;
++
++                                int32_t dx = gx + col;
++                                int32_t dy = gy + row;
++                                if (dx &lt; 0 || dx &gt;= (int)ctx-&gt;buf_width ||
++                                    dy &lt; 0 || dy &gt;= (int)ctx-&gt;buf_height)
++					continue;
++
++				// Blend
++				uint32_t dst = pixels[dy * stride + dx];
++				uint8_t inv = 255 - a;
++
++				uint8_t r_dst = (dst &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF;
++				uint8_t g_dst = (dst &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF;
++				uint8_t b_dst = (dst) &amp; 0xFF;
++
++				uint8_t r_src = (color &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF;
++				uint8_t g_src = (color &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF;
++				uint8_t b_src = (color) &amp; 0xFF;
++
++				uint8_t r = (r_src * a + r_dst * inv) / 255;
++				uint8_t g = (g_src * a + g_dst * inv) / 255;
++				uint8_t b = (b_src * a + b_dst * inv) / 255;
++
++				pixels[dy * stride + dx] = (r &lt;&lt; 16) | (g &lt;&lt; 8) | b;
++			}
++		}
++
++		pen_x += slot-&gt;advance.x &gt;&gt; 6;
++	}
++}
++
++static void bgtk_draw_widget(BGTK_Context* ctx, BGTK_Widget* w) {
++	switch (w-&gt;type) {
++	case BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL:
++		// Draw label background
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h, BGTK_COLOR_BG);
++		// Draw text (offset for simple padding)
++		bgtk_draw_text(ctx, w-&gt;data.label.text, w-&gt;x + 5, w-&gt;y + 5, BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);
++		break;
++	case BGTK_WIDGET_BUTTON:
++		// Draw button background
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h, BGTK_COLOR_BTN);
++		// Draw button border (1px black)
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, 1, BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);            // Top
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y + w-&gt;h - 1, w-&gt;w, 1, BGTK_COLOR_TEXT); // Bottom
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, 1, w-&gt;h, BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);            // Left
++		bgtk_draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;x + w-&gt;w - 1, w-&gt;y, 1, w-&gt;h, BGTK_COLOR_TEXT); // Right
++
++		// Calculate text offset for rough centering
++		// NOTE: A proper implementation would use FT_Get_Text_Width()
++		int text_width;
++		int text_height;
++		measure_text(ctx-&gt;ft_face, w-&gt;data.button.text, &amp;text_width, &amp;text_height);
++
++		// Draw text
++		int offset_x = (w-&gt;w - text_width) / 2;
++		int offset_y = (w-&gt;h - text_height) / 2;
++		bgtk_draw_text(ctx, w-&gt;data.button.text, w-&gt;x + offset_x, w-&gt;y + offset_y, BGTK_COLOR_WHITE);
++		break;
++	}
++}
++
++static void bgtk_draw_widgets(BGTK_Context* ctx) {
++	// 1. Clear the screen
++	bgtk_clear_buffer(ctx, BGTK_COLOR_BG);
++
++	// 2. Draw all widgets
++	for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; ctx-&gt;widget_count; i++) {
++		bgtk_draw_widget(ctx, ctx-&gt;widgets[i]);
++	}
++}
++
++static int bgtk_handle_input_event(BGTK_Context* ctx, struct InputEvent* ev) {
++	// Only handle mouse button presses for now
++	if (ev-&gt;code != BTN_LEFT || ev-&gt;value != 1) {
++		return 0;
++	}
++	printf("BGTK Got click: (%d, %d)\n", ev-&gt;x, ev-&gt;y);
++
++	// Hit-testing for buttons
++	for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; ctx-&gt;widget_count; i++) {
++		BGTK_Widget* w = ctx-&gt;widgets[i];
++
++		if (w-&gt;type == BGTK_WIDGET_BUTTON) {
++			// Check if click coordinates are within button bounds
++			if (ev-&gt;x &gt;= w-&gt;x &amp;&amp; ev-&gt;x &lt; (w-&gt;x + w-&gt;w) &amp;&amp;
++			    ev-&gt;y &gt;= w-&gt;y &amp;&amp; ev-&gt;y &lt; (w-&gt;y + w-&gt;h)) {
++				printf("BGTK Clicked in button\n");
++
++				// Trigger callback
++				if (w-&gt;data.button.callback) {
++					w-&gt;data.button.callback();
++					return 1;
++				}
++			}
++		}
++	}
++	return 0;
++}
++
++static int bgtk_handle_events(BGTK_Context* ctx) {
++	struct BGCEMessage msg;
++	ssize_t bytes;
++
++	// bgce_recv_msg is blocking. This makes the UI reactive.
++	bytes = bgce_recv_msg(ctx-&gt;conn_fd, &amp;msg);
++	if (bytes &lt;= 0) {
++		if (bytes == 0) {
++			fprintf(stderr, "bgtk_main_loop: Server closed connection.\n");
++		} else if (errno != EINTR) {
++			perror("bgtk_main_loop: bgce_recv_msg");
++		}
++		return -1; // Exit loop
++	}
++
++	switch (msg.type) {
++	case MSG_INPUT_EVENT:
++		return bgtk_handle_input_event(ctx, &amp;msg.data.input_event);
++	case MSG_BUFFER_CHANGE:
++		// TODO: Handle buffer resize/move
++		return 1; // Redraw
++	default:
++		// Ignore other messages for now
++		return 0;
++	}
++}
++
++void bgtk_main_loop(BGTK_Context* ctx) {
++	bgtk_draw_widgets(ctx);
++	bgce_draw(ctx-&gt;conn_fd);
++	printf("BGTK Main Loop started. Press Ctrl+C to exit.\n");
++
++	while (1) {
++		int result = bgtk_handle_events(ctx);
++		if (result == -1) {
++			break; // Server error/disconnection
++		} else if (result == 1) {
++			printf("BGTK drawing.\n");
++			bgce_draw(ctx-&gt;conn_fd);
++		}
++	}
++}
++
++// --- Widget Creation Functions ---
++
++void set_label(BGTK_Widget* widget, char* label) {
++	printf("BGTK: setting label: %s\n", label);
++	if (widget-&gt;data.label.text) {
++		free(widget-&gt;data.label.text);
++	}
++
++	char* ptr = calloc(1, strlen(label) + 1);
++	sprintf(ptr, "%s", label);
++
++	widget-&gt;data.label.text = ptr;
++
++	measure_text(widget-&gt;ctx-&gt;ft_face, widget-&gt;data.button.text, &amp;widget-&gt;w, &amp;widget-&gt;h);
++
++	// add padding

++#ifndef BGTK_H

++// Forward declarations

++
++// Function pointer for button callbacks

++
++// BGTK_Context: Holds the state of the BGTK application
++struct BGTK_Context {
++	int conn_fd; // File descriptor for BGCE connection
++	void* shm_buffer;
++	uint32_t buf_width; // The actual width of the buffer (might differ from server width)

++	int width;
++	// FreeType data

++	FT_Face ft_face;
++	int font_size;
++
++	// For now, simple absolute positioning

++	// For now, simple absolute positioning

++	size_t widget_count;
++	size_t widget_capacity;
++};
++
++// BGTK_Widget_Type

++	BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL,

++
++// --- Core Functions ---
++
++// Initializes BGTK, connects to BGCE server, gets buffer/dimensions.
++BGTK_Context* bgtk_init(void);
++
++// Blocking loop to handle events and redraws.
++void bgtk_main_loop(BGTK_Context* ctx);
++
++// Cleans up the BGTK context and resources.
++void bgtk_destroy(BGTK_Context* ctx);
++
++// --- Widget Creation Functions ---
++
++// Creates a label widget.
++BGTK_Widget* bgtk_label_new(BGTK_Context* ctx, char* text);
++
++// Creates a button widget.

++// --- Layout/Management Functions ---
++
++// Adds a widget to the context with absolute positioning.

++
++#endif // BGTK_H
+</pre>

+-// Helper to create a generic widget

+@@ -135,306 +115,9 @@ void bgtk_destroy(struct BGTK_Context* ctx) {
+ 
+ // --- Drawing Primitives &amp; Widgets ---
+ 
+-static void clear_buffer(struct BGTK_Context* ctx, uint32_t color) {
+-	uint32_t* pixels = (uint32_t*)ctx-&gt;shm_buffer;
+-	size_t size = (size_t)ctx-&gt;width * ctx-&gt;height;
+-	for (size_t i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) {
+-		pixels[i] = color;
+-	}
+-}
+-
+-static void draw_rect(struct BGTK_Context* ctx, uint32_t* pixels, int x, int y,
+-		      int w, int h, uint32_t color) {
+-	// Basic clipping and drawing
+-	int x1 = x;
+-	int y1 = y;
+-	int x2 = x + w;
+-	int y2 = y + h;
+-
+-	// Clip to buffer bounds
+-	if (x1 &lt; 0) {
+-		x1 = 0;
+-	}
+-	if (y1 &lt; 0) {
+-		y1 = 0;
+-	}
+-	if (x2 &gt; (int)ctx-&gt;width) {
+-		x2 = ctx-&gt;width;
+-	}
+-	if (y2 &gt; (int)ctx-&gt;height) {
+-		y2 = ctx-&gt;height;
+-	}
+-
+-	int stride = ctx-&gt;width;
+-
+-	for (int j = y1; j &lt; y2; j++) {
+-		for (int i = x1; i &lt; x2; i++) {
+-			pixels[j * stride + i] = color;
+-		}
+-	}
+-}
+-
+-void measure_text(FT_Face face, const char* text, int* out_width,
+-		  int* out_height) {
+-	int width = 0;
+-
+-	for (const char* p = text; *p; p++) {
+-		if (FT_Load_Char(face, *p, FT_LOAD_DEFAULT)) {
+-			continue;
+-		}
+-
+-		width += face-&gt;glyph-&gt;advance.x;  // 26.6 units
+-	}
+-
+-	width &gt;&gt;= 6;
+-
+-	int ascent = face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.ascender &gt;&gt; 6;
+-	int descent = -face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.descender &gt;&gt; 6;
+-	int height = ascent + descent;
+-
+-	*out_width = width;
+-	*out_height = height;
+-}
+-
+-static void calculate_widget_size(struct BGTK_Context* ctx,
+-				  struct BGTK_Widget* w) {
+-	if (!w) {
+-		return;
+-	}
+-
+-	switch (w-&gt;type) {
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL:
+-			if (w-&gt;data.label.text) {
+-				calculate_widget_size(ctx, w-&gt;data.label.text);
+-				w-&gt;w =
+-				    w-&gt;data.label.text-&gt;w + 10;	 // Add padding
+-				w-&gt;h =
+-				    w-&gt;data.label.text-&gt;h + 10;	 // Add padding
+-			}
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_TEXT:
+-			if (w-&gt;data.text.text) {
+-				measure_text(ctx-&gt;ft_face, w-&gt;data.text.text,
+-					     &amp;w-&gt;w, &amp;w-&gt;h);
+-			}
+-			printf("calcutated text size: %ux%u\n", w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h);
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_BUTTON:
+-			if (w-&gt;data.button.label) {
+-				calculate_widget_size(ctx,
+-						      w-&gt;data.button.label);
+-				w-&gt;w = w-&gt;data.button.label-&gt;w +
+-				       20;  // Add padding
+-				w-&gt;h = w-&gt;data.button.label-&gt;h +
+-				       20;  // Add padding
+-			}
+-			printf("calcutated button size: %ux%u\n", w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h);
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_SCROLLABLE:
+-			w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height = 0;
+-			for (int i = 0; i &lt; w-&gt;data.scrollable.widget_count;
+-			     i++) {
+-				struct BGTK_Widget* child =
+-				    w-&gt;data.scrollable.widgets[i];
+-				calculate_widget_size(ctx, child);
+-				w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height +=
+-				    child-&gt;h + 5;  // 5px spacing
+-			}
+-			printf("calcutated scrollable size: %ux%u\n", w-&gt;w,
+-			       w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height);
+-			break;
+-		default:
+-			break;
+-	}
+-}
+-
+-static void draw_text(struct BGTK_Context* ctx, uint32_t* pixels,
+-		      const char* text, int x, int y, uint32_t color) {
+-	if (!ctx-&gt;ft_face) {
+-		// Fallback to simple placeholder if font didn't load
+-		draw_rect(ctx, pixels, x, y, 5, 5, color);
+-		return;
+-	}
+-
+-	// Set font size for drawing context
+-	FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes(ctx-&gt;ft_face, 0, ctx-&gt;font_size);
+-
+-	int pen_x = x;
+-	int pen_y = y + (ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;size-&gt;metrics.ascender &gt;&gt; 6);
+-
+-	int stride = ctx-&gt;width;
+-
+-	for (const char* p = text; *p; p++) {
+-		FT_UInt index = FT_Get_Char_Index(ctx-&gt;ft_face, *p);
+-
+-		if (FT_Load_Glyph(ctx-&gt;ft_face, index,
+-				  FT_LOAD_DEFAULT | FT_LOAD_TARGET_LIGHT)) {
+-			continue;
+-		}
+-
+-		FT_Render_Glyph(ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;glyph, FT_RENDER_MODE_NORMAL);
+-
+-		FT_GlyphSlot slot = ctx-&gt;ft_face-&gt;glyph;
+-		FT_Bitmap* bitmap = &amp;slot-&gt;bitmap;
+-
+-		int gx = pen_x + slot-&gt;bitmap_left;
+-		int gy = pen_y - slot-&gt;bitmap_top;
+-
+-		for (unsigned int row = 0; row &lt; bitmap-&gt;rows; row++) {
+-			for (unsigned int col = 0; col &lt; bitmap-&gt;width; col++) {
+-				uint8_t a =
+-				    bitmap-&gt;buffer[row * bitmap-&gt;pitch + col];
+-				if (a == 0) {
+-					continue;
+-				}
+-
+-				int32_t dx = gx + col;
+-				int32_t dy = gy + row;
+-				if (dx &lt; 0 || dx &gt;= (int)ctx-&gt;width || dy &lt; 0 ||
+-				    dy &gt;= (int)ctx-&gt;height) {
+-					continue;
+-				}
+-
+-				// Blend
+-				uint32_t dst = pixels[dy * stride + dx];
+-				uint8_t inv = 255 - a;
+-
+-				uint8_t r_dst = (dst &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF;
+-				uint8_t g_dst = (dst &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF;
+-				uint8_t b_dst = (dst) &amp; 0xFF;
+-
+-				uint8_t r_src = (color &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF;
+-				uint8_t g_src = (color &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF;
+-				uint8_t b_src = (color) &amp; 0xFF;
+-
+-				uint8_t r = (r_src * a + r_dst * inv) / 255;
+-				uint8_t g = (g_src * a + g_dst * inv) / 255;
+-				uint8_t b = (b_src * a + b_dst * inv) / 255;
+-
+-				pixels[dy * stride + dx] =
+-				    (r &lt;&lt; 16) | (g &lt;&lt; 8) | b;
+-			}
+-		}
+-
+-		pen_x += slot-&gt;advance.x &gt;&gt; 6;
+-	}
+-}
+-
+-static void draw_widget(struct BGTK_Context* ctx, struct BGTK_Widget* w,
+-			uint32_t* pixels) {
+-	switch (w-&gt;type) {
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_LABEL:
+-
+-			// Draw label background
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_BG);
+-			// Draw text widget (offset for padding)
+-			if (w-&gt;data.label.text) {
+-				w-&gt;data.label.text-&gt;x = w-&gt;x + 5;
+-				w-&gt;data.label.text-&gt;y = w-&gt;y + 5;
+-				draw_widget(ctx, w-&gt;data.label.text, pixels);
+-			}
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_TEXT:
+-			puts("drawing text widget");
+-			draw_text(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;data.text.text, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_BUTTON:
+-			puts("drawing button widget");
+-			// Draw button background
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, w-&gt;h,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_BTN);
+-
+-			// Draw button border (1px black)
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, w-&gt;w, 1,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);  // Top
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y + w-&gt;h - 1, w-&gt;w, 1,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);  // Bottom
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x, w-&gt;y, 1, w-&gt;h,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);  // Left
+-			draw_rect(ctx, pixels, w-&gt;x + w-&gt;w - 1, w-&gt;y, 1, w-&gt;h,
+-				  BGTK_COLOR_TEXT);  // Right
+-
+-			// Draw label widget (offset for padding)
+-			if (w-&gt;data.button.label) {
+-				w-&gt;data.button.label-&gt;x = w-&gt;x + 10;
+-				w-&gt;data.button.label-&gt;y = w-&gt;y + 10;
+-				draw_widget(ctx, w-&gt;data.button.label, pixels);
+-			}
+-			break;
+-		case BGTK_WIDGET_SCROLLABLE:
+-			puts("drawing scrollable widget");
+-			// Allocate or update the off-screen buffer if
+-			// needed
+-			if (!w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp) {
+-				int content_height =
+-				    w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height;
+-				if (w-&gt;h &gt; content_height) {
+-					content_height = w-&gt;h;
+-				}
+-
+-				// Allocate the off-screen buffer
+-				w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp = calloc(
+-				    w-&gt;w * content_height, sizeof(uint32_t));
+-				if (!w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp) {
+-					fprintf(stderr,
+-						"Failed to allocate "
+-						"off-screen "
+-						"buffer\n");
+-					break;
+-				}
+-				draw_rect(ctx, w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp, 0, 0,
+-					  w-&gt;w,
+-					  w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height,
+-					  BGTK_COLOR_BG);
+-
+-				// Draw child widgets into the
+-				// off-screen buffer
+-				int current_y = 0;
+-				for (int i = 0;
+-				     i &lt; w-&gt;data.scrollable.widget_count; i++) {
+-					struct BGTK_Widget* child =
+-					    w-&gt;data.scrollable.widgets[i];
+-
+-					child-&gt;x = w-&gt;x + 5;  // 5px padding
+-					if (w-&gt;flags &amp; BGTK_FLAG_CENTER) {
+-						child-&gt;x =
+-						    w-&gt;x +
+-						    (w-&gt;w - child-&gt;w) / 2;
+-					}
+-					child-&gt;y = current_y;
+-					draw_widget(ctx, child,
+-						    w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp);
+-					current_y +=
+-					    child-&gt;h + 5;  // 5px spacing
+-				}
+-			}
+-
+-			// Copy the off-screen buffer to the framebuffer
+-			// according to scroll position
+-			uint32_t* buff = ctx-&gt;shm_buffer;
+-			uint32_t* tmp = w-&gt;data.scrollable.tmp;
+-			for (int row = 0; row &lt; w-&gt;h; row++) {
+-				if (w-&gt;data.scrollable.scroll_y + row &lt;
+-				    w-&gt;data.scrollable.content_height) {
+-					memcpy(
+-					    &amp;buff[(w-&gt;y + row) * ctx-&gt;width +
+-						  w-&gt;x],
+-					    &amp;tmp[(w-&gt;data.scrollable.scroll_y +
+-						  row) *
+-						 w-&gt;w],
+-					    w-&gt;w * 4);
+-				}
+-			}
+-
+-			break;
+-	}
+-}
+-
+ void bgtk_draw_widgets(struct BGTK_Context* ctx) {
+ 	puts("got draw widgets request");
+-	clear_buffer(ctx, BGTK_COLOR_BG);
++	clear_buffer(ctx);
+ 	calculate_widget_size(ctx, ctx-&gt;root_widget);
+ 	draw_widget(ctx, ctx-&gt;root_widget, ctx-&gt;shm_buffer);
+ 	bgce_draw(ctx-&gt;conn_fd);
+@@ -512,23 +195,26 @@ int bgtk_handle_input_event(struct BGTK_Context* ctx, struct InputEvent ev) {
+ 				return 0;
+ 			case BGTK_WIDGET_SCROLLABLE: {
+ 				printf("clicked in a scrollable widget\n");

+ 					    ev.x &lt; (item-&gt;x + item-&gt;w) &amp;&amp;
+ 					    ev.y &gt;= item-&gt;y &amp;&amp;
+ 					    ev.y &lt; (item-&gt;y + item-&gt;h)) {
+ 						printf(
+-						    "clicked in the %d "

++						    "clicked in the %d item\n",
+ 						    i);
+ 						w = item;
++						found = 1;
+ 						break;
+ 					}
+ 				}
++				if (!found) {
++					return 0;
++				}
